recap.back_html: Metadata only: name, shortcuts, OneLake security roles. Not tables or files.
recap.front_html: What Git integration stores for a lakehouse

recap.back_html: Commit exports workspace changes to Git. Update imports Git changes and overwrites the workspace version.
Admin only. Members and Contributors commit and update. Viewers see no Git information.
recap.front_html: Who connects a workspace to Git?

recap.back_html: One workspace per developer on its own branch. Pull requests into main.

lessons.takeaway_html: One workspace per developer on its own branch, pull requests into main, and a data reload plan, because Git holds definitions, not data.
lessons.title: Git integration for Fabric workspaces

recap.back_html: 2 to 10 stages, default Development, Test, Production. One workspace per stage.
Item content and metadata. Not data: refresh models and reload tables after.
Data source, parameter, default lakehouse. Defined in the target stage on the item.
Content is overwritten. ID, URL and permissions stay the same.

lessons.takeaway_html: Stage-specific settings belong in deployment rules. Compare before you deploy. Reload data after, because deployments copy items, not data.
lessons.title: Deployment pipelines, dev to test to production

recap.back_html: Interactive: 5 to 64 minutes. Background: 24 hours. Timepoints are 30 seconds, 2,880 a day.
Up to 10 min: none. 10 to 60: 20 s interactive delay. 60 min to 24 h: interactive rejection. Over 24 h: all rejected.
Capacity level: earlier background rejection. Workspace level: cap a workspace's CU share over 24 hours, except Mission Critical.
Installed by a capacity admin. Health page for throttling. Compute page for 14 days of usage.

lessons.takeaway_html: Know which of your jobs are background, run them off-peak, protect production with surge protection, and read the Metrics app before you resize.
lessons.title: Capacity, smoothing and throttling

recap.back_html: The number in its name: F2 has 2, F64 has 64. Trial capacity has 64.
recap.front_html: Capacity units of an F SKU

recap.back_html: CUs times 30. An F64 has 1,920 CU-seconds per window.
Below F64, every Power BI viewer needs Pro or PPU. From F64, free-licence users with a viewer role can view.
Trial, read the peak in the Metrics app, pick the smallest SKU covering peak plus headroom, scale and check.

lessons.takeaway_html: Measure a real peak on a trial, compare it with each SKU's 30-second budget plus headroom, check the F64 licence floor, then reserve only once the load is steady.
lessons.title: Sizing a capacity, from trial to the right F SKU
